title: Maniram v. State of U.P.
docket: Criminal Appeal Nos. 953 of 2009 and 900 of 2009
disposition: Appeals partly allowed; conviction under s.304-B IPC set aside, convictions under s.498-A IPC and ss.3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act maintained with modified sentences for two of three appellants
headnote: Not a Supply Code case — a dowry-death criminal appeal under IPC ss.498-A/304-B and Dowry Prohibition Act ss.3/4, turning on whether the 'soon before her death' cruelty standard for s.304-B was satisfied. No electricity-related content appears anywhere in the judgment.

holding_units.topic: Criminal appeal against conviction under IPC ss.498-A/304-B and Dowry Prohibition Act ss.3/4 — no Supply Code nexus
holding_units.holding: The Court set aside the s.304-B conviction for want of proximate-in-time cruelty evidence ('soon before her death'), citing Satvir Singh v. State of Punjab, Hira Lal v. State (NCT of Delhi), and Mustafa Shahadal Shaikh v. State of Maharashtra, while maintaining the convictions under s.498-A IPC and ss.3/4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, modifying sentences for two of the three appellants.
holding_units.flag: Recorded for completeness of the source corpus only; no jurisprudential content relevant to the Supply Code.
